notes: Digests and checksums are null in this dev manifest because the scanner images have not been built. Startup validation must therefore treat this bundle as unverified; a release bundle with a null image_digest is a build failure, not a warning. See docs/BLUESCRUB_SUPPLY_CHAIN.md.

tools.name: semgrep
tools.licence_notes: The LGPL applies to the engine. Semgrep-maintained registry rules are under the Semgrep Rules License v1.0, limited to internal, non-competing, non-SaaS use, and are NOT bundled. BlueScrub ships its own pack; an operator may point AIPAM_BLUESCRUB_SEMGREP_CONFIG at registry rules where their use permits it. Verified against 1.175.0: it cannot run under RLIMIT_AS at any value — its OCaml core reserves a large virtual arena — so the external-tool profile sets RLIMIT_DATA instead. Job count is pinned at 4 because its memory need scales with it: on a 32-core host the default is killed at an 8 GiB data ceiling, which would make the scan succeed or fail depending on the machine it ran on.

tools.name: osv-scanner
tools.licence_notes: Tool is Apache-2.0. The OSV advisory data is licensed separately (CC-BY-4.0) and must ship with attribution.

tools.name: grype
tools.licence_notes: Vulnerability database is assembled from distro and language feeds with mixed terms; verify before redistributing the DB alongside the tool.

tools.name: bluescrub_analyzers
tools.licence_notes: Vendored from the private NhanBC/BlueScrub repository. Copyright notices are carried in vendored/. Not redistributable outside this programme.

tools.name: binary_analyzer
tools.licence_notes: Requires pefile, pyelftools, capstone and lief. Each is guarded by an *_AVAILABLE flag upstream, so a missing package yields no findings rather than an error — indistinguishable from a clean binary. The adapter probes get_capabilities() and reports unavailable instead.

tools.name: dependency_inventory
tools.licence_notes: Offline manifest parsing only. Establishes hygiene, not CVE status; reports database_stale when no offline vulnerability source is present.

tools.name: dirty_word
tools.licence_notes: Vendored matcher plus the three shipped packs. Operator wordlists live in bluescrub_wordlists, not on disk. The staged term file is written at mode 0600 and removed after each scan because it holds the markings and codenames being hunted.

tools.name: gitmeta
tools.licence_notes: The adapter is AIPAM's; the analysis is performed by the host's git binary, which is not bundled here — an air-gapped bundle that ships git must carry the GPL-2.0 notice and source offer with it. Only read-only history commands are issued, and the repository's own config is overridden on the command line because several of its keys name programs git would otherwise execute.

tools.name: gitleaks
tools.licence_notes: Engine is MIT. The default rule pack ships with it and is covered by the same licence. `--redact` is deliberately NOT passed: redaction is central, and redacting at the tool would destroy the value before the keyed fingerprint is computed, so two scans of the same secret would stop deduplicating. Its output is therefore plaintext and is written to quarantine/, not beside the findings. Verified end to end against 8.30.1: the `detect --source ... --report-path /dev/stdout` invocation and the bare-array TitleCase report shape are both correct for this version, and a planted GitHub PAT reached the database as a mask plus a keyed fingerprint with the plaintext nowhere in it. Note 8.19+ also offers `gitleaks git` / `gitleaks dir`; `detect` still works and is what the adapter uses.

tools.name: trufflehog
tools.licence_notes: AGPL-3.0. Invoked as a separate process over a pipe, which is not linking, but an air-gapped bundle redistributing the binary must carry the licence and the source offer. Verification is hard-disabled: it proves a credential live by authenticating to the issuing service, which is an outbound connection carrying somebody else's secret from a host with no egress. Asserted by test, not by configuration. NOT verifiable by `go install`: its go.mod carries replace directives, which Go refuses for module installs. It needs a release binary or their install script, so its argv and parser remain tested against recorded output only.

tools.name: build_paths
tools.licence_notes: AIPAM's own detector, no third-party component. Reads build and PDB paths out of strings recovered from compiled artifacts; the source side of the same question is covered by the vendored MetadataLeakageScanner and is deliberately not duplicated.

tools.name: floss
tools.licence_notes: FLOSS is Apache-2.0 and bundles vivisect (Apache-2.0). It emulates the sample's decoding routines, which is why it is emulation class and deep-profile only. **PE only**: verified against 3.1.1, it decodes strings and recovers stack strings for PE and refuses every other format with exit 0, so an ELF or Mach-O artifact is skipped rather than reported as a failed emulation. `--format sc32|sc64` would let it read raw shellcode and is deliberately unused: guessing that a blob is shellcode and guessing its bitness are two guesses, and being wrong emulates nonsense instead of erroring. `--no static` is passed because the static pass has already run in-process and already has the file offsets.

tools.name: binary_indicators
tools.licence_notes: AIPAM's own detector, no third-party component. Extracts network indicators from strings recovered out of compiled artifacts. The vendored binary analyzer can do the same thing with no dependency, but is gated behind pefile/pyelftools and so goes dark on a host without them — which left a hardcoded C2 unreported on the one artifact class this product exists to grade. Only rules measured against a real binary corpus are shipped; mutex, registry and user-agent extraction await a Windows corpus.
